questions.q: What is the typical raw source behind most curated web-text pretraining corpora?
options: Common Crawl snapshots
Hand-typed transcripts from call centers
Only peer-reviewed academic journals
Live social media firehose APIs exclusively
questions.explain: Common Crawl is the largest public web-crawl dataset and the raw source behind most curated web-text training corpora like C4, RefinedWeb, and FineWeb.

questions.q: In what order does cleaned text generally move through the pipeline before training?
options: Tokenize, then filter, then deduplicate, then acquire
Acquire and clean, filter and deduplicate, tokenize, pack, weight and shard
Pack, then acquire, then tokenize, then clean
Shard first, then acquire raw text afterward
questions.explain: The pipeline flows from acquisition and cleaning, through filtering and deduplication, into tokenization, packing, and finally mixture weighting and sharding.

questions.q: Why is `streaming=True` commonly used with Hugging Face `datasets` for pretraining-scale corpora?
options: It makes the tokenizer train faster
It allows reading and transforming data incrementally without materializing the entire multi-terabyte corpus in memory or on disk
It automatically deduplicates the dataset
It converts the dataset into images for vision models
questions.explain: Pretraining corpora can run into terabytes, far exceeding typical local storage; streaming mode reads and processes data on the fly instead of loading it all at once.

questions.q: What is a concrete risk of skipping the deduplication stage of the pipeline?
options: The tokenizer will fail to load
The model wastes compute re-memorizing repeated content, with a risk of test-set contamination
The GPU driver will crash
The vocabulary size will double automatically
questions.explain: Without deduplication, repeated documents cause the model to over-memorize the same content and raise the risk that evaluation data leaked into training.

questions.q: What does the 'packing' stage of the data pipeline do?
options: Compresses the model's weights to reduce file size
Concatenates tokenized documents into fixed-length sequences to minimize wasted padding
Converts tokens back into raw text for human review
Removes toxic content from the corpus
questions.explain: Packing concatenates multiple tokenized documents into fixed-length training sequences so GPU time isn't wasted processing padding tokens that carry no training signal.
